screen: The step counter fades in on the dotted page; “10,000 STEPS A DAY” fades in above it.

screen: A walking figure fades in beside the counter.

screen: “MANPO-KEI” fades in to the right of the counter.
“MAN / 10,000” appears under it.

“KEI / METER” completes the row.

“A NAME, NOT A FINDING” fades in beside the counter.
A timeline draws itself under the counter from “1965” to “2019”; “I-MIN LEE / HARVARD” at the 2019 end; a light travels back along it to 1965.
“BRAND NAME” at the 1965 end; light circles the dial.

camera: carries on right to the next part of the page

screen: The striding legs fade in; “ONE STEP” above them; a light runs down the front leg.
“BIG MUSCLES” to the left; lights travel down both thighs.
A ring circles the front thigh; a magnifying circle grows out to the right showing the thigh muscle; lights run down its fibers on “tighten”; a light circles the knee on “steady”.
camera: shifts right to make room for a lens

screen: A light runs down the back of the hip and thigh; “BACK OF HIP & THIGH”; a thin arrow draws itself forward under the legs.
A ring circles the back calf; a magnifying circle grows out to the left with the calf muscle; lights squeeze up it.
The calf lights up again.
Legs and lens fade; a cut-open vein with two valves fades in; “ONE-WAY VALVES”; both valves glow softly.
The calf muscle fades in beside the vein and gives a small squeeze; lights flow up through the vein; “UP TO THE HEART”.
The upper valve glows as it closes; a light slips down and stops at the valve.
“CALF MUSCLE PUMP” under both; lights rise through the calf and the vein.
“SITTING STILL / ON A LONG FLIGHT”; a slow light settles at the bottom of the vein.
Vein and calf fade; the legs return; lights travel up both legs.
Lights in both thighs; “FUEL?” above.
The camera travels right; footprints walk along the page under it as the legs fade behind.
camera: travels right to the next part of the page

screen: A plate of food fades in, then a sugar cube beside it, then a blood vessel; lights start flowing through the vessel.
More lights in the vessel; “WHERE DOES IT GO?”.
Plate and cube fade; a thigh muscle fades in beside the vessel; a light runs down its fibers.
A thin 100% line draws under them, then a bar fills to 80%; “80% / OF IT WENT INTO MUSCLE” counts up; light in the muscle.
Vessel, muscle and bar fade; an old key fades in; “INSULIN”.
A light slides along the key.
A bundle of muscle fibers fades in to the right; the key fades.
The fiber bundle gives a small squeeze; dots appear along its surface; “SUGAR DOORS / GLUT4”; lights flow into the bundle.
The vessel returns beside the fibers; lights flow from blood into muscle; “WHILE YOU MOVE”.
“TIMING” fades in; two empty boxes draw themselves side by side.
camera: moves down the page to a comparison

screen: “NEW ZEALAND STUDY / TYPE 2 DIABETES” above the two boxes; on “plans” a light runs round each box.
Left box: “30 MIN / ONCE A DAY”, a small walker, and one long bar.
Right box: three small plates appear, each followed by a short bar; “10 MIN × 3 / AFTER EACH MEAL”.
Lights run along both bars; “SAME 30 MINUTES” under the boxes.
Boxes empty; “BLOOD SUGAR AFTER MEALS”; two bars grow — after-meal walking ends about 12% lower; “−12%” counts in.
A thinner third bar grows for dinner; “DINNER −22%”.
Lights rise up both bars.
Charts fade; the blood vessel returns; lights flow through it toward the right.
camera: rises back up to the blood vessel

screen: The camera travels right with footprints walking under it; the vessel fades behind and the heart fades in ahead.
The heart starts a slow, gentle beat; a light flows up the aorta.
A heartbeat trace draws itself beside the heart; “60–100 / BEATS A MINUTE AT REST”; a light runs along the trace.
A second, quicker trace draws itself below the first; “WALKING”.
Traces fade; a thigh muscle fades in to the left; a thin line draws from the heart to it and lights travel along it.
A blood vessel fades in under the muscle and slowly widens; lights pass through; “VESSELS WIDEN”.
Muscle and vessel fade; lights run through the heart; “THE HEART ADAPTS”.
Heart fades; a stethoscope and the empty axes of a chart fade in further down the page.
A blood-pressure line draws itself: steady, a bump during the walk, then lower for a long stretch; “BLOOD PRESSURE”, “BEFORE”, “FOR HOURS”.
“POST-EXERCISE HYPOTENSION”; a light runs along the low part of the line.
A dot marks the dip; “ONE WALK, A SMALL DIP”.
The first line fades; a new one draws three days of walks, each followed by a dip; “MOST DAYS”.
Chart fades; “HOW MUCH?” over open page.
Seven squares (the days of a week) draw in a row; “150 MIN / A WEEK · WHO” counts up.
Each day fills in; “≈ 20 MIN A DAY”.
A small walker fades in at the end of the week; a light rises through it.
Each day's block re-draws as three short pieces.
A light runs across the whole week; “SHORT WALKS ADD UP”.
The camera travels down the page with footprints walking under it; the week fades behind.
camera: travels down the page to the brain

screen: The brain fades in; a light runs along its upper folds.
A ring circles a spot deep in the brain; a magnifying circle grows out to the right showing the curled hippocampus; “HIPPOCAMPUS”.
A seahorse fades in beside the lens; a light traces the hippocampus's curl.
Seahorse fades; lights travel along the hippocampus; “NEW MEMORIES”.
Brain and lens fade; a single hippocampus fades in and slowly shrinks; “SHRINKS WITH AGE”.
Left side: a small walker; “40 MIN · 3× A WEEK / FOR A YEAR”.
Right side: “STRETCHING ONLY”.
A hippocampus appears under each group; a light scans along each one.
The walkers' hippocampus grows a little; “+2%”.
The stretching group's shrinks a little; “≈ −1.4%”.
Top labels fade; “1–2 YEARS TURNED BACK”; a curved arrow turns back beside the walkers' hippocampus.
Five small step counters appear in a row; “78,000 ADULTS / UNITED KINGDOM” counts up.
Step counters fade; two bars grow — the 9,800-step group's bar is half as tall; “−50% / DEMENTIA RISK”.
A middle bar for 3,800 steps grows to three quarters; “−25%”.
Bars fade; the brain returns with an old light bulb beside it; a light runs along the filament.
camera: glides back right to the brain

screen: “81% / MORE CREATIVE WHILE WALKING” counts up; the filament glows again.
An empty rectangle draws itself — the blank wall; “BLANK WALL”.
Bulb and wall fade; lights run through the brain; the camera travels left with footprints walking under it.
camera: travels left to the next part of the page

screen: A nerve cell fades in; “DEPRESSION IS COMMON”.
“A LEADING CAUSE OF DISABILITY / WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION”; a light travels along the nerve cell.
Fifteen small blocks appear in a row; “15 STUDIES”; “191,130 PEOPLE” counts up.
Blocks fade; lights travel through the nerve cell.
Neuron fades; a baseline draws and a light runs along it; a small walker beside “2.5 HOURS A WEEK”; “2.5 HOURS A WEEK / BRISK WALKING”; two bars grow — none vs recommended; “−25%”.
A middle bar for half the activity; “−18%”.
A line draws from the “none” bar to the “half” bar; a light runs down it; “BIGGEST JUMP”.
“STARTING FROM ZERO”; on “zero” the chart fades and a single footprint appears.
“THE FIRST STEPS COUNT MOST”; two more footprints follow.

camera: travels left to the next part of the page

screen: A row of seven small walkers has appeared one by one; “50,225 WALKERS / BRITAIN” counts up.

screen: A long thin line draws under all three — the years of follow-up.
Risk bars grow under the slow and average walkers; the average one is shorter; “−20%”.
The brisk walker's bar grows, shortest of the three; “−24%”.
Walkers and bars fade; a metronome fades in.
A light swings up and down the metronome arm at walking pace; “100 STEPS A MINUTE” counts up.
“MODERATE EXERCISE”.
A footprint appears to the left of the metronome.
A round dial draws above the footprint and a quarter of it fills — fifteen seconds; “× 4”.
“25 × 4 = 100” beside the metronome; the arm glows.
The metronome arm glows once more.
Metronome, dial and footprint fade; two page outlines draw themselves, labelled “2019” and “2020”.

Pages fade; the step counter returns; light circles its dial.

screen: “HOW MANY STEPS?”; a small step counter fades in to the left.
